summary: Built the coverage panel and the five merged fixes as designed. A finished whole-drive scan whose volume figure lands now shows a panel under the unchanged coverage line: the $MFT's valid data length as the one measured part, a remainder labelled 'space this account cannot read' (saying it includes the container layer store when one was left out), the named folders (at most 20 unreadable ones on screen, shallowest first, plus a count; the report holds all), and the files whose own size was not read, kept apart from the unseen space. Everything goes into schema-1 report fields ('coverage', window 'CoveragePanel', OutcomeTexts 'verticalOffset'). A root on a network file system gets no figure, and so no line and no panel. This round fixed the one declared architecture rule the engine found broken: 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends' is an allow-list, and the new Core.Analysis file SizeNotRead.cs, which names ScanStore as its input, was not on it. It now is, with a justification beside LargestFiles and KindBreakdown (it reads a returned store, handed over by the window as ScanResult.Store). No other Core file outside the list names the type (checked), and the rule-copy tests, the architecture tests and the written-once corpus script pass again. The whole suite last passed 1204 of 1204 before that one fitness.yaml edit.

obligations.how: One private Kernel32.OpenRootForQuery (FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES, FILE_SHARE_ALL, OPEN_EXISTING, BACKUP_SEMANTICS) used by IsRemoteRoot and TryGetMftValidData. Per the critic's fix, IsRemoteRoot answers remote when FileRemoteProtocolInfo succeeds or the same handle's final path starts \\?\UNC\. Measured at build on this PC with a FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES open: Z:\ gives FileRemoteProtocolInfo true and final path \\?\UNC\100.109.48.75\collab; C:\ gives false (error 87) and \\?\C:\. Measured too: Windows ignores the share mode of an attributes-only open (a narrowed FILE_SHARE_READ still passed the held-root test), so the share mode itself cannot be told by a test; the single open site is held by the CreateFile count in FailCriticalErrorsTests.

deviations: ScanOptions.VolumeMftReader added (the design named only VolumeSpace.Start's optional mftReader): a scan-level test seam so a Scan can be fed an $MFT figure without reading the real disk; Scanner passes it to Start.

VolumeSpace.Read is composed as Read(root, isRemote, used) with Kernel32.IsRemoteRoot and ReadUsed as defaults, not as a bundle of three probes; the $MFT read stays the separate mftReader because it must run only after a used figure landed.

Kernel32.IsRemoteRoot answers remote on either FileRemoteProtocolInfo or a \\?\UNC\ final path (the critic's fix for O-019, because the info class had never run on a FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES handle). Measured on the real Z:\: both signals agree.

The six E001-* finish-line scripts the design names are not in the tree, so tests/window/SL-001-CoveragePanel.Tests.ps1 (cases A to H) covers their shapes through the published exe; it must be listed as a non-launcher in tests/window/AppArgumentCorpus.json, which an existing rule requires.

No Settings checkbox was added for the mapped-drive rule. GetDiskFreeSpaceExW answering the server volume's figures is its documented meaning, not a defect in Windows, and the old line blaming that gap on this account was this project's own wrong wording, so it is fixed rather than toggled. The existing wcifs-layer-store entry and its checkbox carry the container layer store; the panel names the store as left out beside the figure it changed, and the remainder says it includes it.

The name-clash checker (O-018) reads only the window's own name scope: an x:Name inside a DataTemplate, ControlTemplate, Style or the resources is no field of MainWindow. The real tree showed this (ShareText, a TextBlock in the folder tree's template beside a type of that name); without it the checker gave a false clash.

The mapped-drive probe on this PC's Z:\ runs as an always-on fact (EveryMappedNetworkDriveOnThisPcIsRemoteAndGetsNoFigure) that checks whatever network drives exist and only the local half when there are none, rather than the waived opt-in Z:\ fact (O-020, kept as note N-001).

SizeNotRead.OnDisk takes a ScanStore, as the design says, so the 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore' allow-list in .taad/fitness.yaml now names SizeNotRead.cs beside LargestFiles.cs and KindBreakdown.cs, rather than changing the function to take a ScanResult: the pass is a read of a returned store and the window hands it ScanResult.Store.
not_built: A window run on the mapped Z:\ and a whole C:\ scan with this build: both need the person's allow; they stay person-run (spike clauses b and c; the network pass is stale because MainWindow, Scanning and the hook changed).

The precaution-off position on the real container layer store: scanning it is the kernel leak the precaution avoids, so that position is settled by the unit tests (facts with no NotScanned rows) and by case A, never by a real run.
A window case for a non-NTFS volume or an over-count: no rig here can make either; the unit tests settle them (Build null for unseen < 0; the $MFT reader null).
follow_ups: SC-010 may reuse Kernel32.IsRemoteRoot for the no-offer rule on mapped drives, but never on the UI thread: the open can wait on a dead server (DriveInfo.DriveType is enough for the picker).

Person-run: one non-elevated report-mode scan of the whole C:\ with this build, reading coverage.unseen against measured[0].bytes (spike clause b) and coverage.folders.length (clause c, with the cap of 20 shown), and a window scan of the mapped Z:\ to see no line and no panel.
The network pass (N-001 to N-004 plus StalledShareTests) is stale: this slice touched MainWindow.xaml(.cs), Scanning/** and the hook.
Kernel32.TryFinalPath repeats the buffer logic of SynchronousIoCancel.QueryFinalPath: the volume thread must stay outside the cancel guard, but the two could share one helper.

The three SL-001 fitness entries are not twinned in xUnit (the design's choice); a twin in ArchitectureRulesTests would put them under rules-parity. The 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore' allow-list has no twin either.
The architecture line for C-005 (Core.Analysis) could name SizeNotRead beside the largest files and the kind breakdown.
